A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gaussian-based test-time occupancy framework, despite renaming and substantial extensions. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable. The supplied v1 has no appendix; v2 includes Appendices A.1–A.2, which were included in the comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original occupancy results on Occ3D-nuScenes and nuCraft, component ablations, sensitivity experiments and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: v2 reports original results for LiDAR and camera variants, component ablations, runtime measurements and qualitative analyses, including appendix results.

M1.justification: v2 adds a camera-only pipeline using VGGT depth, triangulation-based scale calibration and RAFT/ego-motion masks to exclude moving regions from accumulation. LiDAR tracking changes from HDBSCAN and ICP-Flow to segmentation-mask association, DBSCAN and ICP. TRBF becomes optional, and Section 3.3 revises its kernel definition and describes color-consistency optimization instead of v1's explicit color-plus-depth objective.

E1.justification: Occ3D-nuScenes and nuCraft remain the benchmarks, with the same driving domain and resolutions. However, v2 evaluates camera-only occupancy on both alongside LiDAR-assisted occupancy, substantially extending the evaluated sensor conditions beyond v1's reported pipeline.

E2.justification: The external comparator sets in Tables 1–2 are retained. VEON is relabeled VEON-LiDAR with unchanged accuracy entries; SelfOcc and C-CONet remain the nuCraft comparators. VGGT and RAFT are pipeline components, not newly evaluated competing occupancy methods.

E3.justification: v2 redesigns ablation controls around single-frame prediction, temporal accumulation and dynamic tracking for both modalities, adding bus, pedestrian and manmade IoUs. It adds per-stage timing measurements and removes the nuCraft IoU and VRAM metrics. Benchmark splits, spatial ranges and resolutions remain unchanged; the newly specified 10% ablation subset does not establish that the subset changed.

E4.justification: The revised ablations isolate how accumulation benefits static content while harming moving objects, and how tracking addresses this. Appendix A.2 revisits TRBF for both modalities; additional figures examine dynamic-mask refinement, denoising and ICP alignment, while Tables 4–5 analyze runtime bottlenecks. v1's iteration/neighborhood sensitivity study and separate SelfOcc temporal-consistency comparison are removed.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its empirical results. v2's runtime averages do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 replace v1's 22.07/8.53 Occ3D/nuCraft mIoU entries with LiDAR results of 23.60/9.08 and add camera results of 13.43/4.33. These accompany method revisions rather than an unchanged-method comparison. Reported LiDAR FPS changes from 2.7/2.6 to 1.9/1.9. SelfOcc's nuCraft mIoU changes from 5.02 to 2.22, matching the mean of its unchanged class scores. Ablation, timing and qualitative results also change substantially.

T1.justification: v1's covariance-weighted spatial and KL-divergence semantic kernels are replaced by a common squared-Euclidean RBF in v2 Equation 5, also used in voxelization. This is a substantive but localized mathematical-definition change. The retained description of covariance-aware voxelization is not reconciled with that replacement equation.

C1.justification: v2 broadens the central contribution to separately evaluated LiDAR and vision-only variants and claims state-of-the-art vision-only performance. TRBF shifts from a central component to optional smoothing. The headline 46% improvement, 2.6 FPS and 56% memory-reduction claims disappear, while the core claims of occupancy prediction without dedicated network training, flexible resolution and open-vocabulary support remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of depth-scale ambiguity, optical-flow error amplification and the decision not to accumulate camera-derived dynamic objects. It contrasts LiDAR sparsity with camera density and depth errors, identifies runtime bottlenecks, and interprets TRBF mainly as visual denoising with negligible aggregate accuracy effects. These considerably revise v1's emphasis on consistent component gains and general temporal coherence.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 supplies previously undocumented details, including 294 × 518 VGGT inputs, triangulation using calibrated cameras, full-resolution OpenSeeD inputs, the segmentation prompt list, mask refinement and instance matching/discard rules. v2 also specifies the 10% ablation subset and runtime accounting. The abstract adds a planned code-release URL, without establishing availability. v1's explicit K=10 recommendation is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for VGGT, RAFT, DBSCAN and classical ICP, while removing the HDBSCAN, ICP-Flow and associated Python/GPU-clustering references. Most research positioning remains intact, with a limited substantive revision explicitly identifying VEON's LiDAR supervision.

P1.justification: The paper is renamed from TT-GaussOcc to TT-Occ and changes its organizing terminology from 'lift-move-voxel' to 'lift-track-voxelize'. The abstract, introduction, method organization, qualitative discussion and conclusion are extensively rewritten, with implementation explanations organized into a new technical appendix.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document from two columns to one, relocates the overview figure, substantially redesigns qualitative comparisons and expands tables for both modalities. It removes the standalone temporal-comparison and sensitivity figures, adds runtime tables and implementation visualizations, and redisplays the main ablations in Appendix A.2 with an additional TRBF row and enlarged views.

improvement.justification: The camera-only evaluation, class-specific accumulation/tracking ablations and implementation/runtime appendix make the method and its evidence easier to assess than in v1. The corrected SelfOcc nuCraft aggregate also improves reporting accuracy. These benefits are tempered by removal of sensitivity and memory evidence and by the unresolved mismatch between covariance-aware voxelization claims and v2's Euclidean kernel equation, supporting a limited net improvement.
